title: Aggregate DMA fences and batch kernel dispatch to cut host CPU overhead
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: The host-side pipeline shows sustained CPU spikes and threadpool contention when handling high fanout prefill workloads and many short decode requests. Root causes identified: (1) thousands of tiny DMA submissions generate individual fence objects and callbacks, flooding the host scheduler; (2) frequent single-kernel launches for short attention/kv operations increase syscall/kernel-dispatch overhead; (3) excessive memcopy task fanout into the threadpool causes lock contention and stalls that amplify tail latency.

Goal: Reduce per-request host CPU overhead (measured as host CPU seconds per 1M tokens) by aggregating DMA fences, coalescing small memcpy work into composite tasks, and introducing a lightweight kernel dispatch batching layer that groups compatible kernel launches. Secondary goals: keep p95 token latency within SLO, preserve throughput, and avoid regressing memory safety or security.

Design proposal summary: 
1) DMA fence aggregation: introduce a host-side DMA fence aggregator that tracks outstanding sub-operations for a logical request and issues a single completion callback when all subops finish. This eliminates O(n) fence callbacks for scattered SG entries and reduces thread wakeups. Implement as a lock-free counter with an optional per-request waiter for compatibility with current synchronous codepaths.
2) Composite memcpy tasks: change the threadpool submission path to accept a small vector of scatter-gather copy ops and perform them in a single runnable to reduce lock acquisitions. For large multi-segment copies we fallback to current strategy.
3) Dispatch batching layer: a thin ring-buffer in the host that groups adjacent kernel launches which are kernel-compatible (same device, stream, compatible launch params) and submits them as a single batched kernel submission where supported by the driver/runtime. When actual fusion is not possible, submit grouped launches back-to-back with one synchronization fence instead of per-kernel fences. Also add kernel selection hints for attention kernels to favor fused-attn variants when sequence length distribution matches.
4) Attention-side micro-optimizations: inline a host-precompute pass that performs rotary/ALiBi bias application for small prefills to reduce separate micro-kernel launches during decode. This is gated behind runtime flags and only enabled when it reduces overall kernel count.

Compatibility and safety: all changes keep a conservative default off gate and are opt-in per deployment. We will provide fallbacks to the previous per-fence behavior for workloads that observe regressions. Thread-safety is validated with stress tests and sanitizers.

Why this is unique: previous tickets focused on single-copy coalescing and scheduler affinity. This work targets the often-overlooked fence/callback storm and groups kernel dispatch at a level that reduces syscalls and scheduler churn without changing GPU kernel semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Host CPU seconds per 1M tokens reduced by >=30% on mixed prefill+decode workload compared to baseline
p95 prefill latency does not regress >10% relative to current SLO baseline
No increase in GPU kernel error rates or correctness failures in nightly regression suite
Feature controllable by runtime flag; fallback path available for quick disable in production
comments: 2026-02-26: Spike: implemented an aggregator PoC using atomic counters. Reduced callback wakeups by ~68% in microbench where 512 small SG entries were used (local perf rig). -- Marco

2026-03-02: Design review with infra and runtime: agreed to make aggregation opt-out for Dedicated customers during initial rollout. Action: add metrics to expose aggregated_fence_count and reclaimed_thread_events. -- Priya (runtime)

2026-03-05: Benchmark run on staging: mixed workload (64-token prefill, 8-token decode fanout) shows host CPU secs/1M tokens from 420s -> 270s (~36% improvement). Observed slight increase in single-request latency p95 for extremely short runs; will add micro-batching heuristic. -- Marco

2026-03-08: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9872 - adds DMA aggregator and composite memcpy task runner. Requesting review from @li-chen for concurrency model and @sandra for packaging rules. -- Ava

2026-03-10: Code review: @li-chen requested additional unit tests around ordering guarantees when aggregator is disabled. Added deterministic stress test. Also recommended switching to futex-wait only in fallback path to avoid busy-wait. -- Marco
measurements: After PoC: 270s (36% reduction) on staging mixed workload
p50 latency unchanged, p95 latency +8% for <4-token decodes in the default heuristic
